findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide ($240-290m, reiterated 2026-08-05) needs >= $138m in H2 after H1 of $102.2m, i.e. ~$69m/quarter against a Q2 run-rate of $50.5m. The Fanapt+Bysanti line ($150-170m) was built 'based on expected BYSANTI launch timing' in H2, but management said at the HC Wainwright conference on 2026-09-15 that the Bysanti launch is 'planned by year-end', so Fanapt alone must carry ~$84.5m in H2 (~$42m/quarter vs $36.0m in Q2). The 'other' line ($80-90m) needs $44-54m in H2 from Hetlioz+Ponvory, which did $35.6m in all of H1 with Hetlioz down 66% y/y. A cut below $240m, or a narrowing to the low end, looks likely against a consensus of $259.7m that still sits near the middle of the range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (revenue $50.5m vs ~$62m expected, guide reiterated): +0.59%. Q1 2026 (miss): -14.11%. Q4 2025: -17.63%. Q3 2025: -20.15%. The name has fallen on 6 of its last 7 prints (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: FY consensus is still $259.66m (Earnings Whispers), above the guide midpoint less the run-rate shortfall, and the buy-side ratings (HCW $20, Oppenheimer $10) were reiterated or initiated after the launch slip. If the cut were fully priced, the FY consensus would sit at or below $240m. Against this, the stock is at its 52-week low and -20% in 20 sessions, which prices some of it.
findings.independence: The launch-timing slip comes from a different source: Quartr summary of the HC Wainwright 28th Annual conference, 2026-09-15 ('BYSANTI launch planned by year-end') https://quartr.com/events/vanda-pharmaceuticals-inc-vnda-h-c-wainwright-28th-annual-global-investment-conference_oS2rUvLL. The H1 numbers and the guide come from the same 8-K exhibit as the reported-quarter finding below.

findings.finding: A bottom-up Q3 build from the Q2 8-K comes to about $60-70m (midpoint ~$65m) against a $68.2m consensus. Inputs: Fanapt ~$38-41m (Q2 $36.0m, +22% q/q, TRx +31% y/y); Hetlioz ~$5-6m base plus the $7.0m of June-shipped orders that the company said moves into Q3; Ponvory ~$8m; Nereus a few $m; Bysanti ~0 (launch 'by year-end'). That is a modest miss of about 4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue missed in Q1 and Q2 2026 (Q2 by 18.6% per Benzinga), and the reactions were -14.11% and +0.59%. Misses have not always been sold once the guide held.
findings.why_not_priced: The $68.2m consensus appears to add the known $7.0m Hetlioz shift on top of a Q2 base that is not repeating (Hetlioz generic erosion) and assumes some Bysanti/Nereus. If the market agreed with ~$65m, the consensus would be there. The bar has a single source, so the size is capped small.
findings.independence: Shares the 8-K exhibit with the guidance finding (same H1 arithmetic, different line). Launch slip: Quartr HCW summary 2026-09-15 (URL above).

findings.finding: Nereus (tradipitant, motion sickness) recognized only $1.0m in Q2: the 10-Q says revenue on initial wholesaler stocking was constrained because high wholesaler inventory made a significant revenue reversal probable. Call summaries put the stocking at $15.2m. If sell-through in Q3 lets part of that constraint release, Nereus could beat; if not, the $10-30m Nereus guide is at risk. Two-sided, with a small positive lean because the constrained revenue is already shipped.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Nereus quarter. Its first quarter (Q2 2026) printed with a +0.59% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The constraint sits in a 10-Q footnote, and the wire carried only the $1.0m net sales figure. A priced release would show in a Nereus estimate above the guide floor, and no such line is published.
findings.independence: The $15.2m stocking figure comes from the Quartr Q2 summary (https://quartr.com/events/vanda-pharmaceuticals-inc-vnda-q2-2026_oS2rUsBK), not from the 10-Q, so it is snippet-level.

findings.finding: The VQW-765 Phase III in social anxiety disorder (546 adults) missed its primary and key secondary endpoints (women SUDS 65.6 vs 66.0 placebo, p=0.89), and the program was put on hold on 2026-10-14. That removes a late-stage R&D line from 2027 spend, in a quarter where opex was $114.3m (R&D $37.0m) and management had already promised opex moderation from late 2026. The call may quantify the savings or reaffirm the runway through end-2027 on lower burn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of an opex-cut announcement at a print in the baseline. The failure itself was absorbed in the October drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: The failure is priced (it is part of the -20% in 20 sessions). The cost saving is not quantified anywhere public. If it were priced, the stock would not be trading at its 52-week low with cash of ~$170m at 2026-06-30 against a ~$237m market cap.
findings.independence: Opex moderation guidance: Q2 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001347178/000162828026053308/vnda8-k852026exhibit991.htm). Program-hold detail: secondary coverage only.

findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price; this finding is the asymmetry it creates. A crowded short at the low means a no-worse-than-feared print moves more upward than the fundamentals alone suggest. If the squeeze were priced, short interest would be falling into the print, not rising.
